title: Read a request from top to bottom
intro: The first line says what to do. Headers describe the message. The body carries the data.
context: Illustrative HTTPS exchange with a fictional /orders endpoint. Authentication headers are omitted for readability; lengths count the ASCII body bytes without a trailing newline.
code:
POST /orders HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 32

{"customer":"C100","quantity":2}

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Location: /orders/4711
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 29

{"id":"4711","status":"Open"}

highlights.label: Send the order
highlights.explanation: POST asks the server to create an order. Content-Type describes our JSON body; Accept asks for a JSON reply.

highlights.label: Read the result
highlights.explanation: 201 says a resource was created. Location points to it, and the response body gives its ID.

outcome: The caller receives order 4711. A 202 response instead would mean accepted for processing, so the caller would still need the eventual result.
caveat: HTTP does not make this endpoint OData. Its URL, payload and error rules belong to the particular API.

title: Repeat a replacement, not an increment
intro: Sending the same desired state twice should not add two more items.
context: Fictional REST endpoint where PUT replaces the complete quantity resource. Two separate identical requests are shown.
code:
PUT /orders/4711/quantity HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 11

{"value":2}

PUT /orders/4711/quantity HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 11

{"value":2}

highlights.label: Set the desired value
highlights.explanation: The request says quantity is 2, not increase quantity by 2.

highlights.label: Retry the same request
highlights.explanation: After either one or two accepted requests, the intended quantity is still 2.

outcome: The operation is idempotent even if the first reply is 201 and the second is 200 or 204.
caveat: A retry can still race with another user. Use the API concurrency rule where needed. POST and PATCH are not automatically safe to retry.

title: See a stale version get rejected
intro: A version token lets the server notice that someone else changed the order.
context: OData V4 example. Another user has already changed order 4711 from version v1 to v2. The client below still sends v1.
code:
PATCH /Orders(4711) HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
If-Match: W/"v1"
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 28

{"Note":"Deliver on Friday"}

HTTP/1.1 412 Precondition Failed
Content-Length: 0

highlights.label: Send the version you read
highlights.explanation: If-Match carries the earlier ETag returned by this OData service.

highlights.label: Reject the stale update
highlights.explanation: The service detects the mismatch. It must not overwrite the newer order with this stale request.

outcome: The client reloads the order and lets the user reconcile changes before sending a new update.
caveat: The weak ETag shown follows OData concurrency rules. Generic HTTP If-Match uses strong comparison. Do not replace the token with * merely to bypass a conflict.

title: Keep a code, a number and null different
intro: These values may look similar on screen, but they carry different information.
context: Original JSON fixture for a fictional order API. The API defines null as clear the note and an omitted note as leave it unchanged.
code:
{
  "customerId": "0000123",
  "quantity": 0,
  "approved": false,
  "note": null,
  "amount": "12.30",
  "currency": "EUR"
}

highlights.label: Preserve the types
highlights.explanation: The customer ID is text with leading zeros. Zero is a number and false is a boolean; neither means missing.

highlights.label: Preserve field presence
highlights.explanation: This message explicitly contains note: null. A mapper that drops presence cannot distinguish clearing the note from leaving it alone.

highlights.label: Follow the amount contract
highlights.explanation: This API uses decimal text plus currency. Convert using the declared precision, not a binary floating-point guess.

outcome: Your ABAP mapping can preserve both the typed value and whether the sender supplied it.
caveat: JSON itself does not define update semantics or a decimal-money type. The clear/unchanged and amount rules above are fictional API rules, not universal JSON rules.

title: Read names, attributes and escaped text
intro: The namespace identifies what an element means. Its prefix is only a short label.
context: Well-formed fictional order document. It is an explanation of XML, not an SAP interface schema.
code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<ord:Order xmlns:ord="urn:example:orders:v1"
           id="4711">
  <ord:Customer>0000123</ord:Customer>
  <ord:Note>A & B <priority></ord:Note>
  <ord:Amount currency="EUR">12.30</ord:Amount>
</ord:Order>

highlights.label: Resolve the namespace
highlights.explanation: ord:Customer belongs to urn:example:orders:v1. Changing ord to a different prefix does not change its meaning if the URI stays the same.

highlights.label: Read text and attributes
highlights.explanation: The note means A & B <priority>. Currency is an attribute on Amount, not part of its numeric text.

outcome: A namespace-aware parser reads the intended customer, note and amount without confusing text with markup.
caveat: Well-formed XML is not proof that it matches the business schema. Configure safe parsing and validate required fields separately.

title: Serialize an ABAP value and read it back
intro: Use a serializer when you need XML, instead of joining strings and escaping characters yourself.
context: ABAP method-body excerpt using the built-in identity transformation. Local demonstration values; no custom objects. Target language-version support must be checked.
code:
CONSTANTS co_note TYPE string VALUE `A & B`.
DATA note TYPE string VALUE co_note.
DATA xml TYPE xstring.
DATA restored_note TYPE string.

CALL TRANSFORMATION id
  SOURCE note = note
  RESULT XML xml.

CALL TRANSFORMATION id
  SOURCE XML xml
  RESULT note = restored_note.

highlights.label: Serialize the value
highlights.explanation: The transformation writes SAP canonical asXML and escapes the ampersand correctly.

highlights.label: Read that format back
highlights.explanation: The same root binding, note, restores the original text into restored_note.

outcome: restored_note contains A & B. XML is the transport representation; it does not alter the note.
caveat: Identity transformation produces asXML, not an arbitrary partner schema. Use a suitable transformation for the partner format and handle CX_TRANSFORMATION_ERROR at the caller. Illustrative, not SAP-executed.

title: Ask for two fields and a small page
intro: The URL tells the service which rows and fields the list needs.
context: Fictional OData V4 Orders entity set with numeric key ID. Each request is separate; the second adds total count for comparison.
code:
GET /Orders?$select=ID,Total&$top=20 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Accept: application/json

GET /Orders?$select=ID,Total&$top=20&$count=true HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Accept: application/json

highlights.label: Limit the list payload
highlights.explanation: $select asks for ID and Total. $top asks for at most 20 rows, not every order.

highlights.label: Notice the extra work
highlights.explanation: The second request keeps the same fields and page limit, then adds the count of matching rows. Measuring that extra work can explain a slow list.

outcome: You can compare response size and backend timings with and without count before blaming the network or Fiori.
caveat: This short URL omits filters and ordering. A real paged list needs stable ordering, and the service must support the requested options. $top does not itself prove the database read is cheap.

title: Filter by status and sort by a stable key
intro: A filter chooses rows. Ordering makes their sequence predictable.
context: Fictional OData V4 Orders model: Status is text and ID is a unique numeric key. The request uses URI-encoded spaces.
code:
GET /Orders?$filter=Status%20eq%20%27Open%27 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Accept: application/json

GET /Orders?$orderby=ID&$skip=20&$top=20 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Accept: application/json

highlights.label: Select matching rows
highlights.explanation: The decoded filter is Status eq 'Open'. This request asks the server for open orders.

highlights.label: Request the next offset page
highlights.explanation: The second, separate request sorts all orders by ID, skips 20, and asks for the next 20.

outcome: You can explain which part changes the result set and which part changes the returned page.
caveat: The two requests deliberately isolate two options; combine them for a filtered paged list. Offset paging can shift when data changes. Follow a supplied nextLink for server-driven paging.

title: Follow nextLink instead of guessing a URL
intro: A page can be smaller than the total result. The server may tell you exactly where to continue.
context: Illustrative OData V4 JSON response to a request that asked for count. The dataset has three matching orders and the server returned the first two.

highlights.label: Separate total from page size
highlights.explanation: The total is 3, but value contains only 2 orders.

highlights.label: Continue using the supplied link
highlights.explanation: Resolve this relative link against the service URL and follow it. Treat the skip token as opaque.

outcome: The client obtains the remaining order without inventing the server paging token.
caveat: V2 uses different count and next-link conventions. The nextLink is not a promise of a frozen snapshot while other users change data.

title: Group two writes in one atomicity group
intro: Being in one batch envelope is different from being in one all-or-nothing group.
context: OData 4.01 JSON batch request body for fictional Orders. Send it to $batch only if the SAP service explicitly supports JSON batch in this version.

highlights.label: Share one group
highlights.explanation: Both writes belong to g1. If one fails, this group must not leave the other write committed.

highlights.label: Keep the envelope separate
highlights.explanation: The two URLs target different orders. Other requests in the batch need not share this transaction boundary.

outcome: The client checks each batch response and the group outcome instead of reading only the outer HTTP status.
caveat: Not a universal RAP wire format. Many SAP services use multipart batch change sets instead. Authentication, CSRF and required If-Match headers must be added according to the actual service.

title: Read the model behind the payload
intro: Metadata tells a client the key and field types before it reads an order.
context: Valid XML CSDL Schema excerpt from a fictional OData V4 $metadata document. The outer edmx document and EntityContainer are omitted.
code:
<Schema Namespace="Demo"
 xmlns="http://docs.oasis-open.org/odata/ns/edm">
  <EntityType Name="Order">
    <Key><PropertyRef Name="ID"/></Key>
    <Property Name="ID" Type="Edm.Int32"
              Nullable="false"/>
    <Property Name="Note" Type="Edm.String"
              MaxLength="80"/>
  </EntityType>
</Schema>

highlights.label: Find the identity
highlights.explanation: ID is the key, is an integer, and cannot be null.

highlights.label: Read the field contract
highlights.explanation: Note is text with a maximum length of 80. A client can use that limit when collecting input.

outcome: Changing ID to a different type or reducing Note to 20 characters can break an existing client.
caveat: This excerpt does not list permissions, behavior or every capability. Read the full metadata and annotations, then verify actual service behavior.

title: Compare a read function with a write action
intro: A function answers a question. An action can change business state.
context: Two separate calls to a fictional OData V4 service. Its metadata declares bound function Demo.CalculateTax and action Demo.Submit.
code:
GET /Orders(4711)/Demo.CalculateTax() HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Accept: application/json

POST /Orders(4711)/Demo.Submit HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 2

{}

highlights.label: Read a calculation
highlights.explanation: The function returns a tax calculation without changing business state.

highlights.label: Request a state change
highlights.explanation: The action asks the service to submit the order. The empty object means this fictional action has no additional parameters.

outcome: A client must treat the submit call as a business operation with possible validation, authorization and concurrency failures.
caveat: These names are not SAP-delivered APIs. Use the actual service metadata, required headers and action parameters. GET must not be used for a hidden posting operation.

title: Separate transport failure from business data
intro: An RFC call can fail before you get a business result.
context: Classic ABAP method-body excerpt. Custom remote-enabled Z_GET_ORDER imports IV_ID and exports ES_ORDER. destination, order_id and typed ls_order already exist. The custom FM has no application exceptions in this illustration.
code:
DATA rfc_message TYPE c LENGTH 255.
CALL FUNCTION 'Z_GET_ORDER'
  DESTINATION destination
  EXPORTING iv_id = order_id
  IMPORTING es_order = ls_order
  EXCEPTIONS
    system_failure = 1 MESSAGE rfc_message
    communication_failure = 2 MESSAGE rfc_message.
DATA(rfc_result) = sy-subrc.
IF rfc_result <> 0.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.

highlights.label: Call a remote-enabled function
highlights.explanation: The destination chooses the connection. Inputs go to the function; outputs come back to the caller.

highlights.label: Capture transport failure immediately
highlights.explanation: Preserve sy-subrc before another statement changes it. The caller cannot treat this branch as a valid order response.

outcome: A successful transport call still needs the business-result checks defined by Z_GET_ORDER. Being RFC-enabled alone does not make it a released BAPI.
caveat: RETURN only illustrates stopping the success path. Production code must report the captured failure and validate authorizations. Custom FM/types are prerequisites; classic RFC usage is not assumed released for ABAP Cloud. Not SAP-executed.

title: Let the outer BAPI caller decide the transaction
intro: Check the BAPI result first. Only its transaction owner decides whether to commit.
context: Classic caller excerpt after a successful local BAPI call. has_business_error was derived from the BAPI-specific RETURN rules. The caller owns this LUW; it is not a RAP handler.
code:
CONSTANTS co_error_types TYPE c LENGTH 3 VALUE 'AEX'.
DATA ls_commit_return TYPE bapiret2.
IF has_business_error = abap_true.
  CALL FUNCTION 'BAPI_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK'.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.

CALL FUNCTION 'BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT'
  EXPORTING wait = abap_true
  IMPORTING return = ls_commit_return.

IF ls_commit_return-type CA co_error_types.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.

highlights.label: Stop on the business error
highlights.explanation: The caller rolls back instead of posting merely because the BAPI call returned normally.

highlights.label: Commit and inspect its result
highlights.explanation: WAIT requests synchronous completion of relevant update processing. The commit result is separate from the earlier BAPI result.

outcome: The caller can distinguish a rejected business request from a failed commit, and report each correctly.
caveat: Failure branches here stop only; add real error reporting. WAIT does not wait for every workflow or remote system. For remote BAPIs, commit must run in the same remote transaction context, not locally. Check API-specific exceptions. Classic API; not permission to commit in RAP. Not SAP-executed.

title: Collect a worker result in its callback
intro: Starting the task and receiving its result happen at different times.
context: Classic ABAP class excerpts. Custom remote FM Z_CALCULATE_PACKAGE exports EV_TOTAL. on_end has one importing character-like task_name parameter; task_id, callback_done, result_code and total are class attributes. The caller permits only a bounded number of active tasks.
code:
CALL FUNCTION 'Z_CALCULATE_PACKAGE'
  STARTING NEW TASK task_id
  DESTINATION IN GROUP DEFAULT
  CALLING on_end ON END OF TASK
  EXCEPTIONS
    resource_failure = 1
    communication_failure = 2
    system_failure = 3.
DATA(start_result) = sy-subrc.

METHOD on_end.
  RECEIVE RESULTS FROM FUNCTION 'Z_CALCULATE_PACKAGE'
    IMPORTING ev_total = total
    EXCEPTIONS
      communication_failure = 1
      system_failure = 2.
  result_code = sy-subrc.
  callback_done = abap_true.
ENDMETHOD.

highlights.label: Dispatch without assuming success
highlights.explanation: A resource failure means the worker did not start. Use bounded retry/backoff rather than flooding the group with more tasks.

highlights.label: Collect the completed task
highlights.explanation: RECEIVE obtains the result or failure. Mark the callback received even on error, then use result_code to decide whether the work succeeded.

outcome: The coordinator tracks start_result separately from result_code and matches each callback task_name to its package.
caveat: Two excerpts, not a complete class. Production code needs per-task storage, start-error handling, timeout and safe retries. Callback completion is not proof of a committed business result. Classic ABAP; not assumed Cloud-released. Not SAP-executed.

title: See why WAIT belongs outside unfinished writes
intro: A waiting coordinator must be designed around database boundaries.
context: Classic method-body excerpt. No pending database writes or open cursor are allowed here. callbacks_received is maintained by aRFC callbacks; tasks_started counts only successfully dispatched tasks.
code:
CONSTANTS co_timeout_seconds TYPE i VALUE 10.

WAIT UNTIL callbacks_received = tasks_started
  UP TO co_timeout_seconds SECONDS.
DATA(wait_result) = sy-subrc.

IF callbacks_received < tasks_started.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.

highlights.label: Use a bounded wait
highlights.explanation: The caller gives callbacks time to arrive and keeps the wait result. It does not wait forever.

highlights.label: Treat missing callbacks explicitly
highlights.explanation: Some tasks may still be running. This path needs recovery or an operator-visible incomplete result, not a success message.

outcome: The coordinator checks each collected worker result after the wait; receiving every callback is different from every worker succeeding.
caveat: Classic WAIT can trigger a database commit. It is not COMMIT WORK AND WAIT and does not prove all business work finished. RETURN stands for an incomplete-outcome handoff. Not a RAP-handler pattern; not SAP-executed.

title: Open, add a step, then release a job
intro: Creating the job header alone does not schedule useful work.
context: Classic method-body excerpt. job_name is TYPE tbtcjob-jobname, job_count is TYPE tbtcjob-jobcount, released is TYPE c LENGTH 1. Custom report Z_RECONCILE is a background-safe report with no mandatory selection parameters.
code:
CALL FUNCTION 'JOB_OPEN'
  EXPORTING jobname = job_name
  IMPORTING jobcount = job_count
  EXCEPTIONS OTHERS = 1.
IF sy-subrc <> 0.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.
SUBMIT z_reconcile
  VIA JOB job_name NUMBER job_count AND RETURN.
IF sy-subrc <> 0.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.
CALL FUNCTION 'JOB_CLOSE'
  EXPORTING jobname = job_name
            jobcount = job_count
            strtimmed = abap_true
  IMPORTING job_was_released = released
  EXCEPTIONS OTHERS = 1.
DATA(close_result) = sy-subrc.

highlights.label: Create the header and step
highlights.explanation: Keep both job name and job count. SUBMIT adds the report as a step of that specific job.

highlights.label: Request release and inspect it
highlights.explanation: An immediate start request still depends on release authorization and available processing resources.

outcome: Use close_result and released to report scheduling status, then use the same job identity to inspect SM37, the log and the business totals.
caveat: Production code must report each error and handle a partially built job; the excerpt stops the failed path only. Finished job status does not prove every record posted. Classic scheduler APIs are not the ABAP Cloud application-job API. Not SAP-executed.

title: Distinguish the envelope from the order data
intro: Control fields describe the interface. Segments carry the actual business values.
context: Teaching-only reduced XML representation of a custom IDoc. ZORDERS01, ZORDER and Z1ORDER are fictional custom definitions; this is not a complete generated IDoc XML schema.
code:
<ZORDERS01>
  <IDOC BEGIN="1">
    <EDI_DC40 SEGMENT="1">
      <IDOCTYP>ZORDERS01</IDOCTYP>
      <MESTYP>ZORDER</MESTYP>
      <SNDPRN>PARTNER_A</SNDPRN>
      <RCVPRN>ERP_100</RCVPRN>
    </EDI_DC40>
    <Z1ORDER SEGMENT="1">
      <EXTERNAL_ID>PO-0071</EXTERNAL_ID>
      <CUSTOMER>0000123</CUSTOMER>
    </Z1ORDER>
  </IDOC>
</ZORDERS01>

highlights.label: Read the control information
highlights.explanation: The basic type describes the segment structure; message type describes the business message. Sender and receiver help select processing configuration.

highlights.label: Read the business data
highlights.explanation: The order segment supplies the external order ID and customer. These values must still pass application checks.

outcome: A wrong receiver or missing partner profile is a routing/configuration problem; an unknown customer is a business-data problem.
caveat: Real control records have additional required fields and generated schemas. Ports, partner profiles and process codes are configuration, not created by this payload. No live IDoc was generated.

title: Separate sent, failed and posted evidence
intro: An outbound success status does not tell you that the receiving system posted an order.
context: Original diagnostic note in JSON, not an SAP wire format or API. The source and receiver have different local IDoc numbers.

highlights.label: Check the sending side
highlights.explanation: Status 03 says data passed to the port. It does not prove that ERP created an order.

highlights.label: Find the receiving business failure
highlights.explanation: The receiver has status 51 and no confirmed application document. Investigate its detailed status messages before retrying.

outcome: Support links both technical messages using the business reference and repairs the customer data or mapping before controlled reprocessing.
caveat: These are common classic status meanings; use detailed messages and actual application evidence. An empty field in a support note is not proof that no document exists. No real customer or IDoc is represented.

references.title: SAP: IDoc communication status and application outcome

title: See structure mapping and value mapping separately
intro: One mapping moves a field. Another translates the value inside it.
context: Original input/expected-output test fixture for a fictional AIF interface. This is not AIF configuration syntax; configure the real interface engine and mappings separately.

highlights.label: Translate the company value
highlights.explanation: The maintained mapping converts EXT01 to 1000. A missing EXT99 mapping must have a defined error path.

highlights.label: Move the reference field
highlights.explanation: Structure mapping puts orderRef into externalOrderId without changing the reference itself.

highlights.label: Test the rejection path
highlights.explanation: A failed mapping must not quietly post to a guessed default company code.

outcome: The operator can identify the source value that needs a mapping fix, then reprocess according to the interface recovery rules.
caveat: Actual AIF processing order depends on its configured engine. Posting still requires business authorization, duplicate protection and correct transaction ownership.

title: Keep delivery ID and business version separate
intro: A new delivery does not necessarily mean a new business command.
context: Original delivery fixture for a fictional approval integration. The same order version was delivered twice with different technical delivery IDs.

highlights.label: Notice the two deliveries
highlights.explanation: Technical delivery IDs differ. Deduplicating only by that ID would allow both to start an approval.

highlights.label: Match the business operation
highlights.explanation: Source, order, version and event identify the same submission in this example. Store the accepted operation durably with its outcome.

outcome: The consumer returns the known approval result for the repeated submission instead of creating a second approval.
caveat: The example key is application-specific. The duplicate check and business effect need a concurrency-safe design; a check followed by an unprotected insert is not enough. For a timed-out remote call, query its known result before replaying.

title: Let a BAdI select the implementation
intro: The application calls a defined extension point, rather than editing the standard implementation.
context: Custom single-use, new-style BAdI illustration. ZBADI_ORDER_CHECK has a COUNTRY filter and interface method CHECK importing IS_ORDER and exporting EV_ALLOWED. order_check is typed REF TO zbadi_order_check; ls_order and allowed match that interface. A fallback implementation is configured.
code:
CONSTANTS co_country TYPE c LENGTH 2 VALUE 'PL'.

GET BADI order_check
  FILTERS country = co_country.

CALL BADI order_check->check
  EXPORTING is_order = ls_order
  IMPORTING ev_allowed = allowed.

highlights.label: Select through the extension definition
highlights.explanation: GET BADI uses the filter value to resolve the configured implementation or its fallback.

highlights.label: Call the agreed method
highlights.explanation: The host supplies an order and receives the decision through the BAdI interface, without knowing the implementation class.

outcome: A different implementation can support another country while the caller continues to use the same interface.
caveat: All Z objects and signatures above are fictional prerequisites. Production code needs the actual BAdI exception and multiplicity rules. A visible BAdI is not automatically released for ABAP Cloud or safe at every transaction point. Not SAP-executed.

title: Read an HTTP response and close on every path
intro: A returned response still needs its HTTP status checked. A connection exception is a different outcome.
context: Method-body excerpt with destination already resolved as an IF_HTTP_DESTINATION reference. The fictional API returns order 4711 as JSON with HTTP 200; /api/orders/4711 is an example path, not an SAP standard endpoint. The enclosing adapter returns the captured outcomes to its caller.
code:
CONSTANTS co_path TYPE string VALUE '/api/orders/4711'.
CONSTANTS co_accept TYPE string VALUE 'Accept'.
CONSTANTS co_json TYPE string VALUE 'application/json'.
CONSTANTS co_timeout TYPE i VALUE 30.
CONSTANTS co_etag TYPE string VALUE 'ETag'.
DATA client TYPE REF TO if_web_http_client.
DATA failure TYPE REF TO cx_root.
DATA cleanup_failure TYPE REF TO cx_root.
DATA status_code TYPE i.
DATA response_text TYPE string.

TRY.
    client = cl_web_http_client_manager=>create_by_http_destination(
      i_destination = destination ).
    DATA(request) = client->get_http_request( ).
    request->set_uri_path( co_path ).
    request->set_header_field( i_name = co_accept i_value = co_json ).
    DATA(response) = client->execute(
      i_method = if_web_http_client=>get i_timeout = co_timeout ).
    DATA(ls_status) = response->get_status( ).
    status_code = ls_status-code.
    response_text = response->get_text( ).
    DATA(etag) = response->get_header_field( co_etag ).
  CATCH cx_web_http_client_error cx_web_message_error INTO failure.
ENDTRY.

IF client IS BOUND.
  TRY.
      client->close( ).
    CATCH cx_web_http_client_error INTO cleanup_failure.
  ENDTRY.
ENDIF.
DATA(read_succeeded) = xsdbool(
  failure IS NOT BOUND AND status_code = 200 ).

highlights.label: Prepare one read
highlights.explanation: Create the released client, select the resource path and request JSON.

highlights.label: Keep response and failure separate
highlights.explanation: Capture status and body if available. Capture client/message exceptions without pretending that an HTTP 404 or 500 is a connection exception. Keep the exact ETag for a later update if the server supplies one.

highlights.label: Close on both paths
highlights.explanation: Close after success or failure. Preserve a separate cleanup error; it must not erase the primary error or change a known server result.

outcome: Only HTTP 200 with no client/message exception sets read_succeeded. The caller must still validate Content-Type and payload before using the order.
caveat: These local outcome variables are a teaching adapter boundary, not a silent error policy: return or map them into your application result and log redacted diagnostics. A cleanup failure is reported separately. The timeout controls this execute call, not every proxy or backend time limit. No automatic retry or SAP execution is shown.

references.title: SAP: Outbound HTTP, destinations and client methods
